OBITUARY REFERENCES  
MR. DEPUTY CHAIRMAN: Hon. Members, I refer with pro found 
sorrow to the passing away of Shri Sriman Prafulla Goswami, 
Shrimati Lalitha Rajagopalan, Shri Ahmad Hossain Mo ndal, Shri 
Kanshi Ram, former Members and Shri Lalit Suri, a s itting Member 
and Shri Santosh Kumar Sahu, a former Member of this House. 
[MR. CHAIRMAN in the Chair] 
Shri Sriman Prafulla Goswami passed away on 27th Ju ne, 2006, 
at the age of 96 years. He represented the State of  Assam in this 
House for two terms from May, 1967 to April, 1972 a nd again from 
April, 1974 to April, 1980. 
Bom at Nalbari, Assam in February, 1911, Shri Goswa mi had his 
education at Cotton College, Guwahati; Jorhat Colle ge and the 
Banaras Hindu University. 
Asocial worker, Shri Goswami participated in the fr eedom 
movement in the year 1921 at a very tender age. He left his studies in 
1930 and started 'Assam Pratishan', an institution for social service. 
He was convicted for joining the Anti-war Satyagrah a movement 
started by Gandhiji and imprisoned and interned sev eral times for 
participating in revolutionary activities in 1941. 
31  

RAJYASABHA [22 November, 2006] 
Shri Goswami was associated with various social, we lfare and 
educational organizations in various capacities and  worked for the 
rural reconstruction and spread of education, espec ially for girls. He 
was instrumental in organizing many Girls' and Boys ' High Schools 
and some dispensaries. He was also President of Gop althan 
Polytechnical Institution in Nalbari sub-division c ontinuously for about 
30 years since its foundation. He was deputed on ma ny occasions by 
the Government of Assam to visit hill areas of Assa m including 
Nagaland, Arunachal Pradesh and Mizoram to study va rious problems 
at the time of crisis till 1964 and also conducted the famous "Naga 
Goodwill Mission" in Assam. Shri Goswami also serve d as the 
Chairman of the Oil India Limited from June, 1972 to June, 1974. 
Shri Goswami was a member of the Indian delegation to the 
Fourteenth Session of the United Nations and was al so part of the 
Indian delegation to the Top management Symposium c onvened by 
the Asian Productivity organization at Tokyo in 1973. 
The Legislative career of Shri Goswami had started when he was 
elected as a Member of the Assam Legislative Assemb ly in 1952. He 
again got elected to that Assembly in 1962. 
In the passing away of Shri Sriman Prafulla Goswami , the country 
has lost a veteran Parliamentarian and a dedicated social worker. 
Shrimati Lalitha Rajagopalan passed away on the 5th  August, 
2006, at the age of 83 years. 
Bom at Madras in March, 1924 Shrimati Rajagopalan h ad her 
education at Presidency High School, Pachiappa's Co llege and 
Women's Christian College, Madras. 
Shrimati Rajagopalan participated in the Hindustan Scouts 
Movement. She also took a leading part in the stude nts' movement 
during 1942 and attended training camp for relief w ork during the 
Second World War for the evacuees from Burma. Shrim ati 
Rajagopalan was a member of the Goodwill Mission to  Africa in the 
year 1965 and of the Indian Delegation to the Unite d Nations General 
Assembly. 
Shrimati Rajagopalan contributed short stories and articles in 
Tamil in various regional papers. 
Shrimati Rajagopalan represented the erstwhile Stat e of Madras, 
now Tamil Nadu, in Rajya Sabhafrom January, 1965 to April, 1970. 
32  

[22 November, 2006]           RAJYASABHA 
In the Passing away of Shrimati Rajgopalan the coun try has lost a 
noted social worker. 
Shri Ahmad Hossain Mondal passed away on the 8th Oc tober, 
2006, at the age of 79 years. He represented the St ate of West Bengal 
in this House from July, 1975 to July, 1981. 
Born at Bankra in the Howrah district of West Benga l in February, 
1928, Shri Mondal had his education at the Calcutta  University and 
Aligarh Muslim University. 
An advocate by profession, Shri Mondal was associat ed with 
various social welfare activities. He was Vice-Pres ident of the Indian 
Red Cross Society. 
The legislative career of Shri Mondal started with the membership 
of the West Bengal Legislative Council where he was  elected in the 
year 1964. Thereafter, he was elected to the West B engal Legislative 
Assembly in the 1967. 
A widely travelled person, Shri Mondal represented the country in 
the United Nations Coference on Trade and Developme nt at Nairobi, 
Kenya in the year 1976 and at International Red Cro ss Conference at 
Bucharest, Romania, in the year 1977. 
In the passing away of Shri Ahmad Hossain Mondal, t he country 
has lost a distinguished social worker and an able Parliamentarian. 
Shri Kanshi Ram passed away on the 9th October, 200 6, at the 
age of 73 years. He represented the State of Uttar Pradesh in this 
House from July 1998 to July 2004. He was leader of  the B.S.P. in the 
Rajya Sabha during this period. 
Born at Khawaspur village in the Ropar District of Punjab in 
March, 1934, Shri Kanshi Ram had his education at G overnment 
College, Ropar. 
Asocial worker, journalist and a writer, Shri Kansh i Ram was 
actively associated with the Dalit movement throughout the country 
and he mobilised them into a formidable political f orce in several 
States. He founded the Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) in  the year 1984 
and remained its national President for almost two decades. 
33 

RAJYASABHA [22 November, 2006] 
 
The legislative career of Shri Kanshi Ram started w ith the 
membership of the Tenth Lok Sabha when he got elect ed in 1991. He 
was again elected to that House in the year 1996. 
In the passing away of Shri Kanshi Ram, the country  has lost a 
noted political personality, a dedicated social wor ker and a champion 
of Dalit movement. 
Shri Lalit Suri passed away on the 10th October, 20 06 at the age 
of 60 years following heart attack. He represented the State of Uttar 
Pradesh in this House for two terms from November, 2002 to July, 
2004 and July, 2004 till his untimely demise. 
Born at Rawalpindi, now in Pakistan, in April 1947,  Shri Suri had 
his education at Sri Ram College of Commerce, Delhi  University and 
Vauxhall Motors, U.K. 
An industrialist by profession, Shri Suri was also a dedicated 
social worker and involved in various charitable ac tivities for providing 
free facilities to pilgrims. 
A Diploma holder in Automobile Engineering, Shri Su ri switched 
over from automobiles to the hospitality business a nd rose to become 
one of the country's leading entrepreneurs in touri sm and hospitality 
sector. He established a network of hotels in vario us parts of the 
country and became the Chairman-cum-Managing Direct or of the 
Bharat Hotels Limited. He was also the President of  the Hotel 
Association of India. 
Shri Suri was instrumental in accelerating the pace  of growth of 
tourism industry in India. He was honoured by the G overnor of Jammu 
and Kashmir for promoting tourism in the State, des pite disturbed 
conditions there. He was also awarded World Travel Market Global 
Award, 2002, for promoting international cooperation through tou rism 
and National Tourism Award 2002-2003 from the Government of India 
for promoting tourism. Shri Suri was also the recip ient of several other 
prestigious awards namely, Hind Rattan, Udyog Rattan, Rajiv Gandhi 
Excellence Award and Excellence as Top CEO Award.  
A keen sports lover, Shri Suri was interested in golf, cricket and 
hockey. 
Shri Suri also brought out an afternoon newspaper n amed Delhi 
Midday.  
34 

[22 November, 2006] RAJYA SABHA 
 
In the passing away of Shri Lalit Suri, the country  has lost a 
distinguished personality. 
Shri Santosh Kumar Sahu passed away on the 2nd Nove mber, 
2006, at the age of 71 years. 
Born at Baripada in the Mayurbhanj District of Oris sa in 
December, 1935, Shri Sahu had his education at M.P. C. College, 
Baripada; and Ravenshaw College and Madhusudan Law College, 
Cuttuck. 
An Advocate by profession, Shri Sahu was actively a ssociated 
with various social welfare and cultural organizati on. He took keen 
interest in the development of sports, co-operative s, economic 
planning and cultural activities. 
Shri Sahu was elected President of the Orissa State  co-operative 
Union in the years 1972,1977 and 1981. He also serv ed as President 
of the Orissa Sahitya Akademi, Orissa Sangeet Natak Akademi and 
Orissa Lalit KalaAkademi from 1963 to 1965; Orissa 
BlindmenAssociation, from 1976 to 1979; and Urban C o-operative 
Bank Institution, Bhubaneshwar, from 1988 to 1990. 
A keen sports lover, Shri Sahu served as President of the Orissa 
Cycling Association. He was also President of the A ll Orissa Volleyball 
Association from 1976 to 1981. 
Shri Sahu started his distinguished legislative car rer with the 
membership of Orissa Legislative Assembly. He also served as a 
Deputy Minister in the State Government of Orissa from 1962 to 1967. 
Shri Sahu represented the State of Orissa in this H ouse for three 
consecutive terms, from April, 1976 to April 1982, from April, 1982, to 
April 1988 and again from April, 1988 to April, 199 4. He was also 
nominated on the panel of Vice-Chairman, Rajya Sabh a during 1984 
to 1986. 
Shri Sahu attended the International Students' Conf erence held 
in Sri Lanka in 1956; Cultural Exchange Programme h eld in the 
U.S.A. in 1968 and Indo-Soviet Cultural Friendship Programme held 
in the U.S.S.R. in 1972. He was also a Member of th e Parliamentary 
Delegation to Zambia in 1980. 
In the passing away of Shri Santosh Kumar Sahu the country 
has lost a distinguished Parliamentarian. 
35

We deeply mourn the passing away of Shri Sriman Pra fulla
